title: World's Best Ski Slopes
description: Test your knowledge of epic ski destinations worldwide

questions.prompt: In which U.S. state would you find the ski town of Aspen?
questions.explanation: Aspen sits in the Rocky Mountains of central Colorado and comprises four mountains — Aspen Mountain, Aspen Highlands, Buttermilk, and Snowmass (Wikipedia: 'Aspen, Colorado').

questions.prompt: Which season pass gives access to Vail, Whistler Blackcomb, Park City, and Breckenridge?
questions.explanation: The Epic Pass, sold by Vail Resorts, covers its owned mountains including Vail, Whistler Blackcomb, Park City, and Breckenridge (epicpass.com; Wikipedia: 'Epic Pass').

questions.prompt: The pyramid-shaped Matterhorn looms over which Swiss ski resort?
questions.explanation: The car-free village of Zermatt sits directly beneath the 4,478 m Matterhorn (Monte Cervino) on the Swiss–Italian border (Wikipedia: 'Zermatt').

questions.prompt: On a North American trail map, which symbol marks the easiest beginner runs?
questions.explanation: North American resorts rate trails by symbol: green circle (easiest), blue square (intermediate), black diamond (advanced), and double black diamond (expert) (Wikipedia: 'Piste § North America').

questions.prompt: Which British Columbia resort hosted the alpine skiing events of the 2010 Winter Olympics?
questions.explanation: The 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics held their alpine events at Whistler Creekside, on Whistler Mountain in British Columbia (Wikipedia: 'Alpine skiing at the 2010 Winter Olympics').

questions.prompt: The resort town of Chamonix sits at the base of which mountain, the highest in the Alps?
questions.explanation: Chamonix-Mont-Blanc lies beneath the 4,808 m Mont Blanc, the Alps' highest peak, and hosted the first Winter Olympics in 1924 (Wikipedia: 'Chamonix').

questions.prompt: Which of these resorts is NOT on the Epic Pass?
questions.explanation: Vail, Heavenly, and Stowe are all Vail Resorts mountains on the Epic Pass; Aspen Snowmass is an Ikon Pass destination owned by the Aspen Skiing Company (Wikipedia: 'Epic Pass', 'Ikon Pass').

questions.prompt: The fearsome Hahnenkamm 'Streif' downhill, one of ski racing's most dangerous World Cup courses, is held in which Austrian town?
questions.explanation: The Hahnenkamm races run each January on the Streif course above Kitzbühel, Austria — its near-vertical Mausefalle start is infamous on the World Cup circuit (Wikipedia: 'Hahnenkamm (Kitzbühel)').

questions.prompt: A 'couloir' — like Jackson Hole's notorious Corbet's Couloir — refers to what kind of terrain?
choices: A wide, gently groomed beginner slope
A steep, narrow gully running between rock walls
An artificial jump in a terrain park
questions.explanation: A couloir is a steep, narrow gully flanked by rock. Corbet's Couloir at Jackson Hole, Wyoming, is entered via a mandatory drop-in and is one of North America's most famous expert lines (Wikipedia: 'Couloir', 'Corbet's Couloir').

questions.prompt: Whistler Blackcomb has the greatest lift-served vertical drop in North America — roughly how much?
questions.explanation: Blackcomb Mountain's vertical drop is about 5,280 ft (1,609 m) — a full mile — the largest of any resort in North America (Wikipedia: 'Whistler Blackcomb').

questions.prompt: Which California resort hosted the 1960 Winter Olympics, the first Winter Games televised in the United States?
questions.explanation: Squaw Valley, near Lake Tahoe, hosted the 1960 Winter Olympics — the first carried on U.S. television (by CBS). The resort was renamed Palisades Tahoe in 2021 (Wikipedia: '1960 Winter Olympics', 'Palisades Tahoe').

questions.prompt: St. Moritz, the only town to host the Winter Olympics twice, lies in which Swiss Alpine region?
questions.explanation: St. Moritz sits in the Engadin valley of canton Graubünden and hosted the Winter Olympics in 1928 and 1948 (Aosta Valley is in Italy, not Switzerland) (Wikipedia: 'St. Moritz').
